severity_criteria.source_excerpt: protocolSection.eligibilityModule.eligibilityCriteria; criterion 4: "4." "Moderate to severe psoriasis as defined at Baseline by:" "* PASI score of 12 or greater, and" "* IGA mod 2011 score of 3 or greater (based on a static scale of 0 - 4), and" "* Body Surface Area (BSA) affected by plaque-type psoriasis of 10% or greater." -- The registry states all three baseline eligibility thresholds. The PASI and IGA scale ranges are directly stated in the eligibility text; BSA is represented as percentage affected.

prohibited_concomitant: Treatments listed in Table 5-1 that could confound efficacy are prohibited after randomization for any indication (including psoriasis), except topical corticosteroids and other topical treatments during maintenance when all stated conditions apply: started after the Week 12 visit was completed, used for 14 consecutive calendar days or less, for an indication other than psoriasis, and not on an area affected with psoriasis.
permitted_concomitant: After screening, psoriasis concomitant medication in all body regions is restricted to bland emollients and other non-medicated interventions not listed in Table 5-1.

During the maintenance epoch, topical corticosteroids and other topical treatments are allowed only when started after completion of the Week 12 visit, used for 14 consecutive calendar days or less, for an indication other than psoriasis, and not on an area affected with psoriasis.
There is no restriction on antihistamines or corticosteroids in the eye, nose, or ear.
value.population_note: Subjects with chronic plaque-type psoriasis, with or without psoriatic arthritis comorbidity.

" Secukinumab 300 mg regimen group: secukinumab 300 mg s.c." " Secukinumab 150 mg regimen group: secukinumab 150 mg (one injection of" " Placebo group: placebo secukinumab (two placebo injections per dose) once per week for" "The use of the treatments listed in Table 5-1 is prohibited AFTER randomization for any" "indication, including psoriasis." "During the screening, subjects will be allowed to use some active topical treatments for any" "indication in the following body regions: face, scalp, and genito-anal area." "treatments are limited to: mild or moderate potency CS." "indication at any time after randomization except as specified in the footnote for Table 5-1." "After the screening the use of concomitant medication for psoriasis in all body regions is" "restricted to bland emollients (not supplied by Novartis) and other non-medicated" "interventions (not listed in Table 5-1)." "Table 5-1 Prohibited treatment" "Topical treatment which is likely to impact the signs and 2 weeks" "symptoms of psoriasis (e.g., corticosteroids[CS], vitamin D" "analogues, pimecrolimus, retinoids, salicylvaseline, salicylic" "acid, lactic acid, tacrolimus, tar, urea, -hydroxy or fruit" "acids)d,e, f" "f Topical corticosteroids and other topical treatments will be allowed during the maintenance epoch" "only if (all must apply):" "•medication was started after the Week 12 visit was completed;" "•medication was used for 14 consecutive calendar days or less;" "•medication was used for an indication other than psoriasis and not on the area affected with" "psoriasis." "There is no restriction on the use of anti-histamines and on the use of corticosteroids in the" "eye, nose or ear." -- The protocol restricts psoriasis concomitant medication to bland emollients/non-medicated interventions after screening, while Table 5-1 treatments generally remain prohibited after randomization. multiplicity_control.source_excerpt: 2.5.2 Primary analysis methods; graphical testing strategy: "A randomized, double-blind, placebo controlled," "PASI 75 response @ Week 12 (compared to placebo) primary" "IGA 0/1 response @ Week 12 (compared to placebo) primary" "One-sided p-values will be derived." "The family-wise error will be set to α=2.5% (one-sided)." "In essence, the type-I-error probability will be equally split for both sets of hypotheses and" "Within each pair of hypotheses (H1 or H3) and (H2 or H4) each hypothesis is tested at α/2." "Only if both hypotheses of a pair are rejected, the testing sequence will continue and the PASI" "90 comparisons of secukinumab versus placebo are tested, H5 or H6 will be tested at α/2 (one-" "If all hypotheses within a set referring to a secukinumab dose regimen have been rejected, i.e.," "(H1, H3, and H5) or (H2, H4, and H6), the corresponding type-I-error probability can be passed" "on to the other group of hypotheses, and if needed, hypotheses can be retested at a new" "significance level." "within each set the hypotheses are tested sequentially as follows:" "The graphical approach of Bretz et al." "Bretz F, Maurer W, Brannath W, Posch M (2009) A graphical approach to sequentially rejective" -- The SAP explicitly describes one-sided family-wise error control at 2.5%, equal initial allocation across the two dose hypothesis sets, sequential testing within dose sets, and recycling after all hypotheses in a set are rejected. Alpha per dose is 0.025 divided equally across two sets (0.0125). The schema supports the graphical procedure enum, so procedure is graphical. testing_sequence remains empty because the hierarchy is conditional rather than one fixed sequence. SAP references identify the trial's co-primary endpoints as PASI 75 and IGA 0/1 at Week 12; the task's schema supports these endpoint labels. The decimal alpha values are conversions of the stated 2.5% alpha and the stated equal split across two sets (2.5% / 2 = 1.25%, or 0.0125). The three hypotheses in each dose set are explicitly enumerated as H1/H3/H5 and H2/H4/H6. The familywise_error_controlled=true assertion is supported by the explicit family-wise error setting; alpha_recycling=true by the stated transfer of alpha; and gatekeeping_structure=true by conditional sequential testing within dose sets.
